proposals.before: Chen Huiji, whose style name was Yuanfang, was a great-grandson of the Founder on the collateral line.
proposals.after: Chen Huiji, whose style name was Yuanfang, was a grandnephew of the Founder on the collateral line.
proposals.reason: 從孫 means collateral grandson/grandnephew of the Founder, not great-grandson.

proposals.before: In the first year of Zhenming, Xiao Yan, prince of Ping'an and left vice director of the masters of writing under Xiao Cong, Xiao Fan, prince of Jinxi, and others[3] led more than twenty thousand followers, men and women together, to offer surrender to Huiji, who marched out with troops to receive them.
proposals.after: In the first year of Zhenming, Xiao Yan, prince of Anping and left vice director of the masters of writing under Xiao Cong, Xiao Huan, prince of Jinxi, and others[3] led more than twenty thousand followers, men and women together, to offer surrender to Huiji, who marched out with troops to receive them.
proposals.reason: 安平王 is Prince of Anping (not Ping'an); 蕭瓛 is Huan, not Fan.

proposals.before: At Hankou he was blocked by the army of the Prince of Qin and could not advance; he therefore joined Xiao Shuwen, prince of Jinxi and prefect of Xiangzhou, Bi Bao, prefect of Bazhou, and others in offering surrender.
proposals.after: At Hankou he was blocked by the army of the Prince of Qin and could not advance; he therefore joined Shuwen, prince of Jinxi and prefect of Xiangzhou, Bi Bao, prefect of Bazhou, and others in offering surrender.
proposals.reason: 晉熙王叔文 is the Chen prince Shuwen, not a Xiao; the Xiao surname is invented in the English.

decisions.reason: 高祖之從孫 marks Huiji as a collateral grandson/grandnephew of the Founder (same generation as 孫). Great-grandson would be 曾孫; the proposed grandnephew restores the correct kinship.
安平王 is Prince of Anping (安平), not Ping'an (平安). 蕭瓛 romanizes as Xiao Huan (瓛 huán), not Fan. Both proposed corrections match the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 安平王蕭巖、晉熙王蕭瓛

decisions.reason: 晉熙王叔文 names the Chen prince Shuwen with no 蕭 surname. Xiao Shuwen was invented by confusion with earlier 蕭瓛; dropping Xiao restores the source.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0001 shows English great-grandson came only from the bad idiomatic of 從孫; the kinship claim must read grandnephew while keeping generationDistance 2, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
Accepted r0002 shows Prince of Ping'an came only from reversing 安平; the title claim must read Prince of Anping while keeping zh, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
Accepted r0002 shows English Xiao Fan came only from the bad romanization of 蕭瓛; the personal-name claim must read Xiao Huan while keeping zh, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
